changes.old_text: Inheritance and abstract classes define stable polymorphic contracts.
changes.replacement_markdown:
Inheritance reuses and specializes a base-class contract; abstraction exposes the required behavior while leaving a concrete subclass to supply its implementation. In X++, a derived class uses `extends` and can have one superclass. An abstract class cannot be instantiated; a concrete subclass must implement its abstract methods. An overridden instance method keeps the inherited signature, and dispatch follows the actual object even when a variable has the base type. See [X++ inheritance](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/dev-ref/xpp-inheritance) and the [abstract modifier](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/fin-ops-core/dev-itpro/dev-ref/xpp-syntax).

For an original adjustment-policy design, let an abstract policy require a calculation and let two concrete policies provide distinct rules. For a synthetic base amount of 100, let one policy return a fixed 5 and the other 10 percent (10). Pass each through the same base-typed consumer and predict those distinct results without branching on concrete class names. In a developer environment, implement and test both variants, then confirm that instantiating the abstract base or omitting a required implementation fails compilation. This is an uncompiled design exercise; inheritance is distinct from wrapping an existing method with CoC.
changes.execution: proposed original design/learner check only; no compilation or tenant execution

affected_wording: Create and modify temporary tables for optimization purposes
changes.old_text: InMemory and TempDB tables have different scale/join/lifecycle behavior.
changes.replacement_markdown:
Choose temporary-table storage from the workload. `InMemory` is an indexed temporary dataset outside SQL Server; it can suit a small working set, while joining it is not a server-side SQL join. `TempDB` stores temporary data in SQL Server and supports joins to regular tables, indexes and TTS transaction scope. See [temporary-table choices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/apply-basic-performance-optimization-finance-operations/3-table).

For an original reconciliation preview, create a temporary AOT table with company, reference and amount fields, choose its `TableType`, and add an index for the measured lookup. Compare a small local working set with a larger dataset joined to application records. Populate and query each using identical filters/totals; verify the buffer instance reaches the consumer. Microsoft documents `setTmpData` for InMemory and `linkPhysicalTableInstance` for TempDB, so substituting one linking mechanism for the other is a failure case. See [temporary-table construction](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/apply-basic-performance-optimization-finance-operations/temporary-tables). Record company isolation, cleanup and measured cost; neither type is durable business storage or automatically faster. No table was built or benchmarked here.

affected_wording: Set up default dimensions for account types
changes.replacement_markdown:
An account-type default applies across a category of accounts; an individual account default can replace that type default. On Dimensions, select the dimension and open **Account Type Default Dim.** to configure the relevant type, value and Value Posting rule. For an original example, suggest department SERVICE for the chosen account type, give one specific account a REPAIRS default and compare the resulting journal lines. Use Code Mandatory with a blank value when a value is required without choosing one automatically; check documented batch-job restrictions before enforcing such rules. See [default dimensions and priorities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/finance-dimensions).

Priorities resolve competing sources per source code, rather than changing the account-versus-type override. Configure the source code and source priorities, then test customer/item/location conflicts and both header-first and line-first entry. Inspect actual line dimensions and any overwrite prompt before posting. This is a proposed sandbox check, not an executed configuration.

Default-dimension priorities resolve competing defaults.

affected_wording: Create and modify fixed assets, main assets, and components
changes.old_text: A fixed asset may be a main asset with components, but component behavior and disposal/acquisition must be tested explicitly.
changes.replacement_markdown:
A main asset groups separately created component assets; it is different from assigning a class/subclass for classification or a depreciation book for valuation. For an original production-line example, create separate fixed-asset cards for the line and its motor, assign the appropriate books before acquisition, then open **Main Asset Components** on the line and select the motor's FA No. Inspect the resulting main/component fields, and deliberately configure **Allow Posting to Main Assets** in Fixed Asset Setup for the intended posting design. See [asset cards and component setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/fa-how-acquire).

Test adding an existing component and changing the component list in a disposable company. Reconcile each card's acquisition, depreciation and ledger history; grouping does not by itself establish that costs were acquired, transferred or depreciated. Compare this component relationship with an ordinary shared asset class. No asset or component transaction was posted here.

#### A resolution dialog is configuration plus permissions

For an original repair-code requirement, first select the customizable resolution dialog in Case Settings. Edit the **Case Resolution** form in Power Apps, add the required repair information, save and publish, then resolve a synthetic case as the representative. Test a custom role as well as the standard role: the environment-variable definition privileges differ between the configuring manager and the representative. If adding a new resolution choice, keep the numeric values aligned between Case status reason and Case Resolution resolution type. A label alone does not establish that relationship. Do not add Regarding to this dialog; Microsoft documents that as unsupported. See [resolution-dialog configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/modify-case-resolution-dialog).

Evidence should include the saved form, role assignment, displayed choices and resulting resolution record. An absent choice can be a value mismatch or publishing issue; a permission failure needs a role correction, not broader access to customer records.

Create a solution-owned Repair Authorization table only if a separate authorization record is justified. Configure an “Awaiting decision” view with decision/expiry conditions and useful case/reference columns. Add the fields and a related-record subgrid to the appropriate form, then save and publish. Use **SendAppNotification** from a supported API/flow path for the specific approver, with a case link and expiry. Notifications target individual users, so a team needs one notification per intended user. Test sender and recipient privileges, duplicate triggering and the denied case link. The Power Apps Notification connector's mobile push is a different mechanism. See [app settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/app-properties) and [in-app notification implementation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/send-in-app-notifications).

Create a **case-type email template** for a repair acknowledgment; choose organizational versus personal availability, supply subject/body and insert supported dynamic values with fallback text. For a monthly 600 expense, create a periodic-journal line with account/offset/dimensions, next date, a one-month interval and the correct last retrieval date. A cutoff spanning several due dates can create the line several times. Retain the periodic definition and the generated journal/voucher separately. Refresh the journal context, enter synthetic lines, publish and inspect validation errors in Finance before posting. Publishing is not posting. A custom workbook's presence on disk does not make it a journal-menu template: promotion has a registration/resource path and journal-type/account-type filtering. proposed_changes.old_text: ## 2. Implement receivables, credit, collections, and subscription billing
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
#### Configure the consolidation company before running it

Create the target legal entity with the financial-consolidation designation, configure its chart, fiscal calendar, accounting/reporting currencies, rate type and exchange rates, then prepare subsidiary account mapping. Choose an elimination company/control design deliberately. A consolidation entity is not a daily operational company. In a synthetic two-subsidiary run, record source dates, account mapping, translation accounts and consolidation history; reconcile source balances before eliminating reciprocals. See [consolidation-company preparation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/prepare-company-for-consolidation). **VERIFY CURRENT:** Consolidate online template and preview behavior; a source balance change requires a deliberate rerun/review, not an unexplained plug.

#### Work a tax intersection through settlement

Set up tax main accounts/posting group, authority and settlement period before linking a code to the period and posting group. Put the appropriate codes in the party sales-tax group and item sales-tax group, then test their intersection on a document. For an invented exclusive-price line of 800, a common 5% code produces 40; an additional code present in only one group does not apply merely because it exists. Review the transaction's calculated tax and any supported documented adjustment, including the configured exemption treatment. See [sales-tax components and calculation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/indirect-taxes-overview).

For settlement, select the settlement period/date interval and correct original/correction processing, review the calculated liability, then run Settle and post sales tax and reconcile the clearing/settlement account. A later tax payment is a separate cash transaction. Test a late invoice after the original settlement and use the documented correction process rather than settling the original interval twice. See [sales-tax settlement procedure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/tasks/create-sales-tax-payment).

Withholding has its own setup. For the **global withholding** mechanism, configure authority, settlement period, ledger posting group/accounts, codes, party groups and item withholding groups before testing the applicable threshold and transaction. Do not assume ordinary vendor-payment withholding and global/localized withholding share every field or calculation trigger. See [global-withholding setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/general-ledger/set-up-global-withholding-tax). For an original paper test, an explicitly applicable 2% withholding on a 1,000 base gives 20 withheld and 980 paid; confirm the actual jurisdiction, taxable base, recognition event and payable/withholding vouchers in an authorized sandbox. This arithmetic does not establish a real tax rate or policy. **VERIFY CURRENT:** localization, tax-engine selection, account requirements, rounding and feature state.

proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
#### Generate recurring invoices and process collection evidence

Create a free-text invoice template containing the service/revenue account, amount, tax/charges, terms and dimensions; assign it to the customer with start/end, frequency and any maximum amount. Generate for a chosen invoice date, inspect the recurrence ID and individual documents, submit workflow when required, validate and post. A generated recurrence group is not a posted receivable. See [recurring free-text invoice setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/accounts-receivable/set-up-process-recurring-invoices).

For a prepayment scenario, configure the prepayment posting account/feature and applicable parameters, create/confirm the proposal and post the deposit invoice, then settle it through the customer payment journal. Select the received prepayment for application to the final sales invoice and verify synchronous settlement or successful background application under the configured option. For a 5,000 sale with an agreed 1,000 deposit, reconcile a 4,000 remaining receivable, then test reversal/credit. See [customer prepayment setup and application](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/accounts-receivable/customer-prepayment-invoice). **VERIFY CURRENT:** line-level versus header-level prepayment and settlement feature/parameter state. A payment journal marked as a prepayment is not automatically the same contract as a sales-order prepayment invoice.

Billing classification has public-sector applicability: create the classification with terms, associate existing billing codes and explicitly decide interest/collection-letter settings; the documented defaults suppress those activities for that classification. Apply it to an appropriate free-text invoice and verify grouping and due date. See [billing classification setup](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/public-sector/tasks/create-billing-classification-public-sector). Do not treat it as a universal customer-payment category.

For letters, assign the collection sequence and permission on the customer posting profile, generate the selected transaction/date/customer population, review the created letter, then print/post under the intended process. Customer-level versus transaction-level handling changes how letters group and advance. See [collection-letter processing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/accounts-receivable/tasks/process-collection-letters). For interest, assign the interest code to the applicable posting profile, select the calculation population/date range, review created notes and post with the intended per-transaction versus grouped posting behavior. See [interest-note processing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/accounts-receivable/tasks/process-interest). In both cases, test a payment or credit arriving before posting; stale selection must not produce an unjustified demand. Retain source open items, calculation parameters, note/letter ID and voucher.

For mileage, configure the rate/tiers and test quantities immediately below/at/above a tier boundary and the fiscal-versus-calendar accumulation setting. For per diem, confirm the intended interface/feature, travel dates/location and included-meal reduction method before calculating. proposed_changes.old_text: ### Codeunits, events and interfaces
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
### Worked object path: import, query and report

For a synthetic compliance register, keep imported staging data separate from posted business records. In an [XMLport](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-xmlport-object), declare the format/direction and a root text element containing a table element. Put record fields in field elements or attributes according to the external schema. Set the table view and linking properties deliberately; call the XMLport from a page action or codeunit, with the chosen import/export direction and request-page behavior. Inspect the exported structure, then reject a missing required identifier in an import test. Parsing a file successfully does not prove that its business records are valid. Keep this worksheet on synthetic staging data and preserve the existing transaction/error rules.

For a [query object](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-query-object), nest the child dataitem beneath its parent, set `DataItemLink` and `SqlJoinType` on the lower item, and select only needed columns. Declare the intended output grain before adding aggregation. In calling AL, set runtime filters, open the query, read each result and close it. A changed join can remove unmatched parents or multiply rows; reconcile the fan-out example before replacing record loops.

Build a [report dataset](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-report-dataset) from dataitems/columns, with child links, request filters and labels. If a query supplies the rows, iterate it into the report's dataset rather than assuming the layout can directly consume an arbitrary query. Design the [report object](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-report-object) in dataset → request page → rendering → code order; bind Word/RDL/Excel layout fields to that dataset. Test a document header with zero, one and several lines, translated labels, request filters and totals. A processing-only report omits rendered output but still needs observable results. **Answer check:** correct layout with duplicated dataset amounts remains incorrect. These are implementation design steps, not compiled or server-tested AL; verify current syntax/runtime before building.

proposed_changes.old_text: ## 5. Work with development tools
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
### Worked AL reasoning: values, variables and record effects

Trace a procedure before running it: define two `Decimal` inputs for quantity and unit price, a local `Decimal` subtotal and a Boolean validity result. Initialize the subtotal, reject a negative quantity with an `if` branch, calculate quantity times price with an arithmetic expression, and return the result. A caller passing an ordinary value does not receive a mutation to its variable; use a `var` parameter only when changing the caller's value is part of the contract. Local variables belong to the method; object-global variables belong to the object. [AL variables](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-al-variables) have typed initialization and assignment/conversion rules. Text that looks numeric still needs a supported conversion, and overflow remains an error.

Now separate a scalar calculation from record work. A record variable represents a table and current filters/state; set the filter, retrieve the intended record set, then decide whether a field needs `Validate` before `Modify`. A loop that changes persisted records needs a transaction and concurrency decision; it is not equivalent to updating the local subtotal. Predict zero quantity, a negative input, a failed conversion and a missing record, and inspect which state can change in each case. This is an original paper trace, not a compiled AL sample; use the earlier error/commit model when adding persistence.

For document automation, an instant cloud flow can accept a synthetic file, pass File Content to AI Builder's [Process documents](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ai-builder/form-processing-model-in-flow) action using a trained/published model, and pass extracted values to a review or storage step. Retain both a field's value and confidence score; extracted amounts are strings and need validated conversion before numeric use. A low-confidence or inconsistent total should enter a review branch rather than authorize payment. This is API/cloud document processing even though the input began as a scanned document. **VERIFY CURRENT:** AI Builder capacity, model and file support; do not submit private documents for practice.

UI/browser work can produce a recorder placeholder that must be replaced with actual recorded or manually authored actions. proposed_changes.old_text: ### Operate Microsoft Security Copilot with the same rigor as other privileged tooling
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
### Worked ingestion path: direct Windows events versus WEF

For a disposable Windows source, install the appropriate Content Hub solution and open its connector. Confirm workspace and deployment permissions, select or create a DCR, associate the intended Azure VM or Arc-enabled machine, choose the event set or a tested XPath filter, and select the destination workspace. With [Windows Security Events via AMA](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/connect-services-windows-based), trace a harmless known sign-in event into `SecurityEvent` and inspect its computer, event ID and timestamps. A DCR existing without the intended machine association does not prove collection.

For [Windows Event Forwarding](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/sentinel/windows-security-event-id-reference), first prove WEC is receiving the subscribed events locally, then configure AMA/DCR on the collector and verify `WindowsEvent` ingestion. Do not expect an unchanged analytics rule querying `SecurityEvent` to match records held only in `WindowsEvent`. Adapt its query or use an appropriate parser, then test a known source event through the detection. Common, Minimal, All and Custom sets differ; Minimal is not a full audit trail, and All here is not every Windows log. Preserve source event identity and compare source/ingested counts before evaluating detection coverage. **Answer check:** a healthy collector with no incident can be a table/query mismatch rather than event loss. **VERIFY CURRENT:** connector/portal support, table schemas and permissions. No collector or analytics rule was deployed in this review.

proposed_changes.old_text: ### Distinguish message masking, voice masking and recording controls
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
### Worked conversation lifecycle rule

For a synthetic messaging workstream, use [timeout rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/configure-time-out-rules) to choose customer or representative nonresponse, threshold/unit and a supported action. Start with a localized warning message and explicit fallback language; then model close, wait or release-to-queue behavior where supported. Set the rule active, bind it to the correct workstream, set priority and test which party sent the last message. Voice and AI-only conversations are outside this timeout-rule feature. Do not confuse this per-workstream automation with the service's [automatic closure scheduler](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/auto-close-conversation-powerapps), which uses conversation state and `modifiedon`; consultation/transfer can recalculate its elapsed time. Do not repair it by directly editing Dataverse state/status.

**Answer check:** a live-chat customer waiting after their own message does not meet a customer-nonresponse condition that starts after the representative's message. Record the expected transition, message language, capacity change and re-entry behavior. Recheck documented channel/state support and observed timing before treating a threshold as an exact closure promise. **VERIFY CURRENT:** rule availability and scheduler behavior. This is a tabletop exercise, not a tenant observation.

proposed_changes.old_text: ### Configure voice agents
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
### Worked representative-assistance setup

For a pilot persona, enable the intended Copilot experience and make it available through the applicable experience profile. In the [help-pane configuration](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/contact-center/administer/copilot-enable-help-pane), enable Ask a question, configure approved knowledge and then set preset, representative-selectable or automatic filters deliberately. A hidden preset filter is not the same as a visible representative choice. Test an article inside the selected scope, one outside it and a user without source access; a filter does not replace authorization.

For [conversation summaries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/contact-center/administer/copilot-enable-summary), select the supported join/transfer/end or on-demand triggers rather than assuming all occur automatically. Check the documented deployment applicability; case-summary configuration has a different scope. In [Manage format](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/contact-center/administer/customize-copilot-conv-summary), choose paragraph or structured output, add only needed information sections, and omit information not present in the conversation. Test a transcript that lacks an error code; an invented code fails acceptance even if the summary reads fluently.

For the measured plugin/tool extension, the current [Copilot Studio extensibility procedure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/customer-service/administer/extend-copilot-with-copilot-studio) is **preview**. Enable the extension in Customer Support settings, configure the agent's tool/knowledge in Copilot Studio, review passed context and publish/test the intended version. Existing plugins can continue to work; edits beyond connection/description may require a replacement tool. **Answer check:** successful summarization does not prove the custom tool was invoked—basic summarization takes priority over extensibility. **VERIFY CURRENT:** licenses, regional prerequisites, deployment applicability and settings. No tenant or agent changes were made here.

proposed_changes.old_text: An unhandled error normally aborts the current uncommitted database work; it does not undo earlier commits or remote effects. A caught [try-method error](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-handling-errors-using-try-methods) is different: database writes in that method are not automatically rolled back. Consuming the Boolean return catches the error; calling the same attributed procedure without consuming its return behaves like an ordinary call. Online permits writes inside try methods, while on-premises blocks them by default. Keep recoverable parsing/validation separate from writes.
proposed_changes.replacement_markdown:
An unhandled error normally aborts the current uncommitted database work; it does not undo earlier commits or remote effects. A caught [try-method error](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-handling-errors-using-try-methods) is different: database writes in that method are not automatically rolled back. Consuming the Boolean return catches the error; calling the same attributed procedure without consuming its return behaves like an ordinary call. Online permits writes inside try methods, while on-premises blocks them by default. Keep recoverable parsing/validation separate from writes.

A less obvious boundary is argument evaluation: the [try-method documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/business-central/dev-itpro/developer/devenv-handling-errors-using-try-methods) evaluates argument expressions inside the try call. A helper that writes a record before returning an argument still performs that write in the try context; the default on-premises write restriction applies there too. Compute write-producing arguments outside the try call only when the resulting transaction boundary is intentional. Moving a write changes error handling; it does not make the whole business operation atomic.
proposed_changes.reason: Adds source-explicit evaluation-order pitfall to safe AL behavior, preserving online/on-prem distinction.
proposed_changes.confidence: Confirmed source behavior; proposed study checks are not executed product evidence

### Focused reading and evidence route

Then allow about 30–45 minutes for an original worksheet comparing a daily sales file, a replicated operational database and a live event stream. For each, draw source → ingestion/reference → store → semantic model → report, explain ETL versus ELT and identify freshness, identity and reconciliation checks. This worksheet estimate covers three scenarios and written justification, not deployment. The [Fabric exercise introduction](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/examine-components-of-modern-data-warehouse/5-exercise-data-analytics-fabric) publishes another 30 minutes and requires a Fabric account/trial; its launched instructions were unavailable in this review.
